record.paper_title: Open Problems on Configuration Spaces of Tensegrities
record.original_question: In the planar Cayley-algebra description of tensegrity strata, determine when two Cayley algebra systems define the same stratum or the same stratum condition; here the Cayley-algebra setting uses points and lines in the plane together with the join and meet operations to express geometric conditions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Work in the real projective plane (or affine plane) and consider the planar Cayley algebra whose objects are points and lines. It is equipped with two operations: the join, which to a pair of distinct points associates the line through them and to a point and a line produces incidence relations, and the meet, which to a pair of distinct lines associates their intersection point. By iterating joins and meets starting from a finite list of input points (the "free" generators), one builds compound expressions whose vanishing or incidence conditions translate into polynomial conditions on the coordinates of the inputs.

A Cayley algebra system is a finite collection of such Cayley-algebra expressions/conditions in a fixed set of input points. The zero locus of these conditions in the configuration space of the input points is called the stratum defined by the system; two systems are said to define the same stratum condition if they cut out the same subset of the configuration space (equivalently, the same closed condition up to the chosen notion of equivalence, e.g., set-theoretic equality of strata).

Problem. Give a complete description (e.g., a decision procedure, a normal form, or a set of generating syntactic moves) determining when two planar Cayley algebra systems, built from points and lines via the join and meet operations, define the same stratum, and equivalently when they define the same stratum condition.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying when two planar Cayley-algebra systems define the same stratum is posed as an open problem in the literature on configuration spaces of tensegrities. A targeted web search did not surface a published resolution; related work on Cayley factorization and invariant-theoretic normal forms addresses adjacent questions but does not give a complete equivalence criterion for tensegrity strata.
